ai.title: CLI: Extract shared connection monitor singleton, pause probes during
ai.summary: The adaptive health-check loop is extracted from the `useConnectionStatus` hook into a new process-wide singleton in `cli/src/utils/connection-monitor.ts`, owned by `createConnectionMonitor` with a lazily created instance accessible via `subscribeToConnectionStatus`. The hook now only subscribes to this shared state and reads its callback through a ref so that re-renders with unstable closure identity never reset the backoff timer or fire an extra probe. `use-chat-streaming.ts` calls `setConnectionMonitorBusy(isStreaming || isChainInProgress)` in an effect so the monitor pauses its 5s network probe during an active turn, because the turn's own success or failure is better evidence of connectivity than a concurrent probe. The interval escalation ladder (10s to 10min over 3 to 20 consecutive successes) and exponential failure backoff are preserved verbatim from the old hook.
ai.evidence: The diff moves the adaptive health-check polling logic from `cli/src/hooks/use-connection-status.ts` into a new process-wide singleton in `cli/src/utils/connection-monitor.ts`, and adds `setConnectionMonitorBusy` called in `use-chat-streaming.ts` to pause probes during active streaming. The docstring in `connection-monitor.ts` states that the old hook-level loop reset backoff on every render, which flooded `/api/healthz` (1.17B GETs/week, ~74% of web Render service requests).
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show how the 1.17B GETs/week metric was collected or whether the reduction has been measured post-deploy; the docstring cites it as the historical root cause but no post-fix telemetry is included.

eli5.text: The Codebuff terminal assistant no longer sends constant, unnecessary network pings to check if it is online. It now pauses its automatic connection checks whenever you are actively working with the AI, because the fact that your command is running proves the connection is alive. This is an internal stability fix that stops the app from flooding the service with duplicate requests; it will not change how you use the tool or what you see on screen.

facts: bug: a BYOK session that unsubscribed (its hook takes the early return for `hasSelectedByokConnection`) left this loop polling the Codebuff backend forever, since unsubscribing only removed the listener and never paused the timer.

Registered before any caller awaits `request`, so it runs first and the slot is free by the time a continuation might schedule the next probe. Callers await `request` itself, so sharing adds no extra microtask hops to a check.

The generation may have moved on while this awaited — e.g. the last subscriber unsubscribed mid-check. The reading is still real, so keep it as the snapshot the next subscriber starts from (it is what `lastCheckAt` now vouches for), but a stale loop must not emit or reschedule.
Nobody's listening — pause the loop instead of polling into the void. `started` stays false so the next subscribe() restarts it; `stopped` stays false so it can.

ai.title: Connection monitor pauses polling when no subscribers remain
ai.summary: The CLI connection monitor in `cli/src/utils/connection-monitor.ts` now pauses the health-check loop when the last listener unsubscribes, preventing the timer from continuing to poll the backend indefinitely. This addresses a bug where BYOK sessions that unsubscribed early would leave the monitor running forever. Additionally, an `inFlight` promise is introduced to deduplicate concurrent probes during rapid subscribe/unsubscribe cycles, ensuring that resubscribing adopts a pending check rather than starting a new one.
ai.evidence: In `cli/src/utils/connection-monitor.ts`, the subscribe unsubscribe callback now checks `listeners.size === 0` to pause the loop, and a new `inFlight` variable deduplicates concurrent `checkConnection` calls during fast pause/resume cycles. The test file `cli/src/utils/__tests__/connection-monitor.test.ts` asserts that unsubscribing the last listener pauses the loop and that in-flight checks do not revive it.

eli5.text: The tool that checks whether your connection to the service is still alive now goes to sleep when no part of the app is waiting for its updates. Before this fix, certain sessions that stopped listening early would leave the checker running in the background forever, wasting energy and cluttering your network activity. You will not see any new buttons or settings, but the app will stop making pointless background pings the moment it finishes streaming, making the tool more efficient.

DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Fast is now available to users in limited regions if they have a paid plan, and Space Bunny Alpha no longer carries a Recommended badge in the model list. ai.title: Freebuff admission waits when queue is paused
ai.summary: A new gate function, freebuffChatAdmissionMayStart, in the CLI admission hook now blocks Freebuff chat admission when the user has paused the message queue. The ChatRuntimeProvider replaces its previous inline idle check with a call to this function, passing the queue's paused state. While admission is requested but held back by a paused queue, the chat controls surface FREEBUFF_ADMISSION_QUEUE_PAUSED_MESSAGE instead of the generic 'session starting' text. This mechanism prevents the CLI from buying an unused one-hour session slot for a queue that will not send any messages.
ai.evidence: New export freebuffChatAdmissionMayStart in cli/src/hooks/use-freebuff-chat-admission.ts gates admission with !queue.queuePaused, replacing the inline condition in cli/src/contexts/chat-runtime-context.tsx. When this happens, the interface shows a specific notice instead of the usual 'session starting' message. This affects you, the Freebuff user, by ensuring your session credit is only claimed when the queue is actually ready to send work.

ai.title: Reset cached idle gap on resumed tool exchanges
ai.summary: The agent runtime now refreshes the `sentAt` timestamps of preserved tool exchange messages during context compaction. In `packages/agent-runtime/src/compact-history.ts`, the `compactRequestHistory` function maps the freshly fitted messages to overwrite any existing `sentAt` value with the current time before constructing the final output.
